candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — medication indication and expected outcomes in heart failure
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize the FDA-labeled role of isosorbide dinitrate/hydralazine as adjunct heart-failure therapy in self-identified Black patients and distinguish it from replacement therapy or unrelated drug mechanisms.

options.A: This combination is FDA-approved as adjunct therapy in self-identified Black patients with heart failure to improve survival, prolong time to heart-failure hospitalization, and improve patient-reported functional status.
options.B: The combination is used only for blood-pressure control and has no heart-failure outcome indication.
options.C: The medication replaces all other standard heart-failure therapy once it is started.
options.D: The benefit is based on beta-receptor blockade by hydralazine and calcium-channel blockade by isosorbide dinitrate.

candidate.rationale: The current BiDil prescribing information states that isosorbide dinitrate/hydralazine is indicated as adjunct therapy to standard therapy in self-identified Black patients with heart failure to improve survival, prolong time to hospitalization for heart failure, and improve patient-reported functional status. Therefore, A is correct. B ignores the labeled heart-failure indication, C incorrectly substitutes the combination for standard therapy, and D assigns mechanisms that the components do not have.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Directly supports the labeled adjunctive heart-failure indication and outcomes in self-identified Black patients.
